finding.claim: SSRF in /logo: the only validation is strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") on the raw string. An attacker can pass any URL that contains that substring, e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?x=example.io, http://127.0.0.1:8081/?example.io, or http://example.io.attacker.com/. The server fetches it with http.Get, which follows redirects by default, and streams the full response back to the attacker.
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, response body copied to the client at main.go:38

trace.note: substring check only; the URL is not parsed and the host and scheme are not checked
http.Get(raw) with the default client, which follows redirects
full response body returned to the attacker, so this is a non-blind SSRF

finding.guards_checked: strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is the only control. It is a substring match, not a host allowlist, so it is bypassable via the path, query, fragment, userinfo or a subdomain of an attacker domain. There is no scheme restriction, no private/loopback IP blocking, and no redirect restriction. The /cdn handler's controls (parsed hostname allowlist, no redirects) are not applied here. Not an enforced control.

verdict.guard_found: strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at main.go:32, a substring check that does not close the finding. There is no URL parsing, scheme check, host allowlist, IP blocking or redirect restriction.
verdict.reason: At main.go:31 the unauthenticated `logo` form value flows past only the substring check at main.go:32 into `http.Get(raw)` at main.go:36, with redirects followed and the body returned at main.go:38. The `/logo` route at main.go:43 has no auth, and the strict `trusted` allowlist and `noRedirect` are used only in `cdn` (main.go:20-24).
